I work on the economic evaluation of health technologies, mostly alongside
clinical trials, and on the methods that health technology assessment depends
on. I'm particularly interested in how analytical choices, such as the costing
perspective or the way survival is extrapolated, change the decision a model
supports.

## Areas of interest

- **Trial-based economic evaluation**: cost-utility analysis alongside
  randomised trials, including costing perspective, missing data, and joint
  uncertainty in costs and outcomes.
- **Methods for health technology assessment**: survival extrapolation,
  including cure and spline models, and value of information.
- **Pharmacoepidemiology**: how medicines are used in practice and how external
  shocks change prescribing.

## Selected projects

[CASTLE: sleep in childhood epilepsy]{.project-title}

The NIHR-funded CASTLE programme evaluated an online behavioural sleep
intervention for children with epilepsy in the CASTLE Sleep-E randomised trial.
I contributed to the trial's economic evaluation; the programme's final report
was published in *Programme Grants for Applied Research* in 2026.

[EXPO: extended-release buprenorphine for opioid use disorder]{.project-title}

EXPO was a pragmatic phase 3 trial comparing monthly extended-release
buprenorphine with daily standard-of-care medication. I worked on its
cost-utility analysis, which took a societal perspective, including criminal
justice costs. I now lead an extension of the EXPO economic modelling.

[Survival extrapolation for advanced therapies]{.project-title}

With Dyfrig Hughes I reviewed methods for extrapolating survival in economic
evaluations of advanced therapy medicinal products, where trial follow-up is
short and hazards are complex.

[COVID-19 and primary-care prescribing in Wales]{.project-title}

I developed the analytical strategy for identifying changes in primary-care
prescribing across Wales during the pandemic. The analysis is documented at
[github.com/w-hardy/sercymru](https://github.com/w-hardy/sercymru), with a
companion package,
[serCymruTools](https://github.com/w-hardy/serCymruTools).

## Earlier research

My PhD in sport and exercise psychology used quantitative and machine-learning
methods to study completion of outdoor leadership qualifications
([thesis](https://github.com/w-hardy/thesis)). I have also published on risk
and motivation in high-risk sports.
